evidence.evidence_text: Many recent studies have investigated social biases in LLMs but brand bias has received little attention.
Using a curated dataset across four brand categories, we probe the behavior of LLMs in this space.
Biased models may perpetuate societal inequalities, unfairly favoring established global brands while marginalizing local ones.

We find a consistent pattern of bias in this space—both in terms of disproportionately associating global brands with positive attributes and disproportionately recommending luxury gifts for individuals in high-income countries.
We also find LLMs are subject to country-of-origin effects which may boost local brand preference in LLM outputs in specific contexts.
